claims.harm: Passing an AutoFile across process boundaries complicates IPC and lacks clean separation between GUI and node
claims.quote: if the GUI & node are running in separate processes, it could be a awkward for the gui process to create an AutoFile object and pass it to the node like this.
claims.settled_by_quote: I think b464f388197c5c31937d309d817d38c4b4849a91 is an improvement over previous de11e3b89f8aba9a90a3419086807e5fee0f941d because it passes an fs::path argument from the GUI to the node instead of an AutoFile file argument.

claims.harm: Signaling progress updates per coin will fire over 100 million times on mainnet
claims.quote: This will fire 100 million times during a mainnet snapshot load. Is that overkill?
claims.settled_by_quote: addressed the snapshot load progress notification to batch progress updates for every 100,000 coins processed

claims.harm: Redundant file open and metadata parse in the RPC handler duplicates activate()
claims.quote: If the file can't be opened for reading, or metadata can't be parsed, won't that come up in `activate()` on line 3433?
claims.settled_by_quote: Yes! That duplication is gone in af0c253. File open, metadata parse, and activation all live in SnapshotImpl::activate().

support.reason: tested the mainnet snapshot load with the QML gui branch built on top of this
At first glance this looks very reasonable. I also tested it in the (current) GUI with https://github.com/bitcoin-core/gui/pull/870
The new interface and signal handlers are fairly straight-forward and follow existing patterns. Consuming the new interface in the `loadtxoutset` RPC ensures it is covered by tests.

result.notes: Initial record built. Three non-blocking concerns (IPC path handling by ryanofsky, excessive progress notification emissions by pinheadmz, and RPC duplicate parsing by pinheadmz) were all resolved with pushed revisions.
